_meta.purpose: The head/tail word table ssot-affixes.md §4.12 names for a RARE item (3+ affixes): 'a generated two-word name from a head/tail word table, seeded by roll_seed — Bramble Bite, Havoc Root'. Nothing in data/seed/items/ carried one before 2026-09-06, which is why ItemNameComposer's rareNameDraw had no production supplier and the whole naming path stayed unwired.
_meta.shape: Two independent lists. The draw picks one head and one tail with SeededRng.DeriveStream(roll_seed, 'item.rare-name'), so the same (container_id, catalog_revision, roll_seed) always produces the same name — SC5, the same guarantee the rolls themselves carry, and it survives a reroll unchanged.
_meta.notMechanical: Deliberately decorative and deliberately unrelated to what the item does. §4.12's own reasoning: with up to 6 affixes there is no honest way to compress the item into prefix + noun + suffix, and naming it after two of six would be a lie. Diablo 2's RarePrefix.txt / RareSuffix.txt are the same shape for the same reason. The affix list is the tooltip's job, not the name's.
_meta.tone: Plant / zombie / elemental / decay, matching the corpus's own established voice (Ashen Reliquary, Sunworn Charm, Ember Legion, Kindling, Tidewrack Band, Stillmarch) — never generic high fantasy. words.v1.json's v2 note is the standard: this is a suburb, a garden and a graveyard, not an armoury.
_meta.size: 26 × 26 = 676 pairs. Content, not a tunable — a balance pass has nothing to change here, so there is no data/tuning/ row for the list length (tunables-ssot.md's own test: changing a word changes no behaviour).
